prompt: What is the phase shift of $y = \sin\left(2x - \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$?
hint: You cannot read the shift straight off until the $x$ inside has a coefficient of $1$.

hints.text: You cannot read the shift straight off until the $x$ inside has a coefficient of $1$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up with $y = \sin\left(x - \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$: the $x$ already has coefficient $1$, so you read the shift straight off as $\frac{\pi}{2}$ right. A $2$ in front must be factored out first, which halves that shift.
Factor the $2$ out of the parentheses: $2x - \frac{\pi}{2} = 2\left(x - \frac{\pi}{4}\right)$.
Now it reads as a shift right of $\frac{\pi}{4}$.

explanation: Rewrite the inside in the form $B(x - C)$: $2x - \frac{\pi}{2} = 2\left(x - \frac{\pi}{4}\right)$.
In $y = \sin(B(x - C))$ the phase shift is $C$, here $\frac{\pi}{4}$, and the minus sign sends it right.
So the graph of $\sin(2x)$ slides $\frac{\pi}{4}$ to the right.

alternativeExplanations.title: Find where the cycle starts
steps: A sine cycle begins when its input is $0$: set $2x - \frac{\pi}{2} = 0$.
The cycle that normally starts at $x = 0$ now starts at $x = \frac{\pi}{4}$ — a shift right of $\frac{\pi}{4}$.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: The trap is answering $\frac{\pi}{2}$ to the right (choice B) by reading the number off the end of the expression.
That only works when the coefficient of $x$ is $1$. Here the $2$ compresses everything, so the actual slide is half as big.
Rule: always factor out $B$ first, or solve "inside $= 0$". Both give $\frac{\pi}{4}$, never $\frac{\pi}{2}$.
